July 29, 2026

Report of over 400 US service member deaths in Iran war as strikes hit base in Jordan

tags: war, defence, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @aaronparnas

Data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request to the Defense Manpower Data Center indicates that more than 400 US service members have died in the Iran-US war. An Iranian ballistic missile struck a United States base in Jordan overnight, and Iran launched a surprise attack on American bases in the Middle East despite US claims that Tehran wants to negotiate. China is reported to be supplying Iran with roughly 400 air defense missile launchers valued at $60 million to $70 million. President Trump responded with vulgar language and said the United States would strike Iran extremely hard.

Epstein survivors hand files to senators ahead of Todd Blanche confirmation vote

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

More than 10 Epstein survivors went office to office on Capitol Hill delivering copies of the Epstein files to Republican and Democratic senators, including members of the Judiciary Committee. Offices visited included those of Senators Katie Britt, Mike Lee, Josh Hawley and John Kennedy. The effort targets senators who have declined to read the files and aims to persuade them to vote no on Todd Blanche's confirmation, scheduled for the following day. Survivors say they will continue pressing the issue even if Blanche is confirmed.

Thune says Republicans lack votes for SAVE Act as Trump misses citizenship case deadline

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Senate Majority Leader John Thune confirmed that Republicans do not have the votes to pass the SAVE Act or to eliminate the filibuster. Party leaders may attempt to move the measure through budget reconciliation, but the votes are not currently there, leaving the bill without a path before the November elections. Separately, President Trump's legal team missed the deadline to ask the Supreme Court for a rehearing in his birthright citizenship case, foreclosing that request.

Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment throughout congressional hearing

tags: health, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

Anthony Fauci declined to answer questions at a congressional hearing, invoking his Fifth Amendment rights on the advice of counsel in response to every question, including questions from Senator Rand Paul about gain-of-function research on monkeypox at the National Biodefense Analysis and Countermeasures Center and Fort Detrick, and about whether the CIA transferred funds to the NIH under an interagency agreement. One of his attorneys was ruled out of order for speaking and sitting at the witness table after being told not to, and was escorted from the room. Lawmakers also challenged Fauci over past remarks that making life difficult for unvaccinated people would push them to get vaccinated, and over vaccine requirements imposed by schools and large employers.

CENTCOM warns troops that shared videos help Iran target US bases

tags: defence, surveillance
sources: @oafnation_actual

The top US Middle East commander warned service members that videos they share can help Iran assess the effects of its strikes on American bases. Sources said phone restrictions, including confiscations, are being considered in response.

Defense Department post shows AI prompt asking to build an agent to generate a war

tags: defence, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

A post from the Department of War's official account, promoting new AI task forces embedded within the US Pacific Fleet under the Undersecretary of Research and Engineering, included an image of a service member interacting with an AI chatbot. Zooming in on the image reveals the typed prompt "I need help building an agent to generate a war." The post drew widespread online criticism, with observers debating whether it was deliberate trolling or a lapse in operational security.
